name: Poke
description: Poke offers AI-driven productivity features. GAIA provides a comprehensive open-source productivity OS with 50+ integrations and proactive automation.
metaTitle: Poke vs GAIA: Open-Source AI That Acts First
metaDescription: Poke vs GAIA: Poke answers when asked but never acts first; GAIA triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across 50+ tools. Free tier included.
intro: Poke is a light helper for everyday tasks. It answers questions and assists, but you still direct every step. GAIA works the other way round: an open-source assistant that watches your inbox, calendar, and tasks, then acts on what it finds. It connects 50+ tools and remembers context across them, so follow-through happens without prompting.

rows.gaia: Open-source productivity OS with proactive AI that manages email, calendar, tasks, and workflows
rows.competitor: AI productivity assistant with targeted features

rows.gaia: Monitors your digital life 24/7 and acts before you ask
rows.competitor: Responds to user requests and interactions

rows.gaia: 50+ integrations including Gmail, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Todoist, Asana, Linear
Graph-based memory connecting tasks, meetings, documents, and user preferences
Fully open source with self-hosting via Docker
Multi-step workflows with smart triggers and cross-tool orchestration
Web app, desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux), mobile, Discord, Slack, Telegram bots

gaiaAdvantages: Open source with full transparency and self-hosting
competitorAdvantages: Simpler onboarding for basic productivity needs
Focused feature set may be easier to learn
verdict: Choose Poke if you want a simple helper for small tasks. Choose GAIA if you want an open-source assistant that runs the whole workflow: triaging email, managing calendar and tasks, and automating across 50+ tools without being asked each time.

faqs.question: What makes GAIA different from Poke?
faqs.answer: GAIA is a complete productivity operating system that proactively manages email, calendar, tasks, and workflows across 50+ integrations. It is fully open source and self-hostable, with graph-based memory that learns your work patterns over time.
